headline: TSMC to hike prices for all advanced nodes by 5-10%
summary: TSMC reportedly raising prices for major chip designers. Price hikes to affect 74% of wafer revenue.
details: TSMC has reportedly informed customers to prepare for price increases across its advanced chipmaking portfolio, extending the hikes beyond the newer 3nm process to include 7nm and even legacy products. The exact size of the increases remains unclear, but generally appears to fall in the 5% to 10% range.

The price increases would affect the bulk of TSMC's wafer revenue and could raise costs for major chip designers, including Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm, Broadcom, and MediaTek. 3nm alone accounted for 25% of TSMC's wafer revenue in the first quarter of 2026.

The company's full advanced-node portfolio, defined by TSMC as 7nm and more advanced technologies, accounted for 74% of wafer revenue. The hikes would span nearly three-quarters of the company's wafer business.
TSMC's pricing strategy is strategic, not opportunistic, the company said in a statement. The move also comes as TSMC benefits from a surge in AI-related demand.
caption:
TSMC to raise prices for major chip designers. Will AI demand sustain the price hike?

TSMC has reportedly informed customers to prepare for price increases across its advanced chipmaking portfolio, extending the hikes beyond the newer 3nm process to include 7nm and even legacy products. The exact size of the increases remains unclear, but generally appears to fall in the 5% to 10% range.

The price increases would affect the bulk of TSMC's wafer revenue and could raise costs for major chip designers, including Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm, Broadcom, and MediaTek. 3nm alone accounted for 25% of TSMC's wafer revenue in the first quarter of 2026.

The company's full advanced-node portfolio, defined by TSMC as 7nm and more advanced technologies, accounted for 74% of wafer revenue. The hikes would span nearly three-quarters of the company's wafer business.

TSMC's pricing strategy is strategic, not opportunistic, the company said in a statement. The move also comes as TSMC benefits from a surge in AI-related demand.
